<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin=par72/>only examples found have ''ô'' (not ''û''), viz. {{GHGheb|text=נְפֽוֹצֹתֶם|translate=ye have been scattered}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=11|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=34.41|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וּנְקֹֽטֹתֶם|translate=and ye shall loathe yourselves}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=31|hidebook=1}}.—To the ''ĭ'' (instead of ''ă'') of the preformative may be traced the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נֵעוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=17}} (analogous to the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=נִמּוֹל}}, see below, ee), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵעוֹר}} for ''yiʿʿōr''.—The {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=הִדּוּשׁ}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=10}}; in {{GHGheb|text=לֵאוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=30}}, the Masora assumes the elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לִהֵאוֹר}}); but probably {{GHGheb|text=לָאוֹר}} ({{GHGterm|Qal}}) is intended (see {{GHGpar|51|l}}).—{{GHGheb|text=נַמוֹג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=31}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָסוֹג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=13}} are to be regarded as ''infinitives absolute''.

{{center|III. ''On Hiphʿîl, Hophʿal, and Piʿlēl''.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|w}}
6. Examples of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} without a separating vowel (see above, k), are: {{GHGheb|text=הֵבֵ֫אתָ}}, &c. (see further, {{GHGpar|76|g}}); {{GHGheb|text=הֵמַ֫תָּה}} (from {{GHGheb|text=מוּת}}) for ''hēmáth-tā'' (cf. {{GHGpar|20|a}}); {{GHGheb|text=הֵכַ֫נּוּ}} 1st ''plur. perfect Hiphʿîl'' from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=19}}, even {{GHGheb|text=הֲמִתֶּם}} ({{GHGpar|27|s}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=6}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=28}}, also {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲמִתֶּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=16}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲמִתִּ֫יהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=5}}; but elsewhere, with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵֽמַתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=30}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵֽמַלְתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=16|verse=13}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵֽנַפְתָּ֫}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=24}}, &c.—In these cases the ''ē'' of the first syllable is retained in the secondary tone; elsewhere in the second syllable before the tone it becomes {{GHGheb|text=־ֱ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=12}}, &c.) or more frequently {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}, and in the syllable before the antepenultima it is necessarily {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}} (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲקִֽמֹתִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=18}}). Before a suffix in the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=13}}) and {{GHGterm|fem.}}, and in the 3rd ''plur.'', the vowel of the initial syllable is {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, in the other persons always {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} (König); on {{GHGheb|text=הֲקֵֽמֹתוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=44}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=27|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=4}}, and above, ''i''. The 3rd ''fem. perf. Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֵסַ֫תָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=25}} is quite abnormal for {{GHGheb|text=הֵסִ֫יתָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=סוּת}} or {{GHGheb|text=סִית}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|x}}
As in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} with {{GHGheb|text=ח}} for their first radical ({{GHGpar|67|w}}), all the forms of {{GHGheb|text=עוּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=23}} (where against the rule given under ''i'' we find {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֵדֹ֫תָה}} with ''ē'' instead of ''î''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=19}}, and {{GHGheb|text=עוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, take Pathaḥ in these conjugations instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}. The irregular {{GHGheb|text=וְהֽוֹשְׁבוֹתִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=10|verse=6}} has evidently arisen from a combination of two different readings, viz. {{GHGheb|text=וְהֽוֹשַׁבְתִּים}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}}) and {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲשִֽׁבוֹתִים}} (from {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּב}}): the latter is to be preferred.—On {{GHGheb|text=הֵבִישׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=הוֹבִישׁ}} as a (metaplastic) {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹשׁ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|78|b}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|y}}
7. In the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, besides the short form {{GHGheb|text=הָקֵם}} (on {{GHGheb|text=הָשַֽׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=22}} with Silluq, cf. {{GHGpar|29|q}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=35}} for {{GHGheb|text=הָשַׁב}} read the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הָשֵׁב}}) the lengthened form {{GHGheb|text=הָקִ֫ימָה}} is also found. With ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=הֲקִימֵ֫נִי}}, &c. The {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=18}} is irregular (for {{GHGheb|text=הָבֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=16}}); perhaps {{GHGheb|text=הָבֵיא}} (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=40}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=6}}) is intended, or it was originally {{GHGheb|text=הָבִ֫יאָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|z}}
In the {{GHGterm|infinitive}}, elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} occurs in {{GHGheb|text=לָבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=39|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=10}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לְהָבִיא}}); {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} {{GHGterm|fem.}} is added in {{GHGheb|text=לַֽהֲנָפָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=28}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=18}} and the analogous {{GHGterm|infinitive Haphʿel}} in biblical Aramaic, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=20}}.—As {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=הָכִין}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=14}} (perh. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=23}}).—The {{GHGterm|participles}} have ''ē'', on the analogy of the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, as the vowel of the preformative, like verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67|i}}). On {{GHGheb|text=מֵבִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=2}}, &c. (in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}), see {{GHGpar|74|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|aa}}
On the shortened forms of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} ({{GHGheb|text=יָקֵם}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קֶם}}, but always {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֵ֫א}}; in the {{GHGterm|jussive}} also with retraction of the tone {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תָּ֫שֶׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=20}}) see above, f. With a guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}} the last syllable generally has {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} (as in {{GHGterm|Qal}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫עַד|translate=and he testified}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָרַ֫ח|translate=let him smell}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫רַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫סַר}}<section end=par72/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
